question.problem:
A speedboat travels downstream on a river. The table below gives the speed $v(t)$, in miles per hour, of the boat at certain moments during its journey.

| $t\,(\text{hours})$ | $0$ | $0.5$ | $1$ | $1.5$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)\,(\text{mi/hour})$ | $10$ | $35$ | $40$ | $65$ | $80$ |

Use a left Riemann sum for $v(t)$ over the interval $[0,2]$ with four subintervals to approximate the total distance traveled by the speedboat.

*Hint: The distance traveled is given by the area under the speed-time graph.*
question.worked_solution:
First, let's compute the step size $Δt,$ which is just the width of each rectangle. In this case, the endpoints of our interval are $a=0$ and $b=2,$ and there are $n=4$ rectangles, so the step size is

$$
Δt=\frac{b-a}{n}=\frac{2-0}{4}=0.5.
$$

The area $A$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{v({x}_{0})+v({t}_{1})+…+v({t}_{n-1})}})\cdot \,\,{{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{ }\text{width}} \\  & =(v(0)+v(0.5)+v(1)+v(1.5))\cdot Δt.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $v(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $0$ | $0.5$ | $1$ | $1.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)$ | $10$ | $35$ | $40$ | $65$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(10+35+40+65)\cdot 0.5 \\  & =150\cdot 0.5 \\  & =75\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total distance traveled by the speedboat. So, the distance is $75\,\text{mi}.$
